introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: One and Three Quarter Hours.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Carefully read the excerpt below and answer the questions that follow:

> The people and institutions that combine together to **convert resources into finished products and distribute them to users** collectively form the economic system or the economy.
>
> ..... a modern economy is a complex system. While no two economies are exactly the same, it is possible to identify three types of economic systems or economies.
>
> Each type of economic system is characterised by the role played by its government in taking decisions and influencing the operation of the economy.

*Source: Success in Economics; Chris Nuttall, Derek Lobley; 4th Edition Page 21.*

questions.enonce_markdown: Which economic term best describes the underlined phrase in the excerpt? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The phrase **"convert resources into finished products and distribute them to users"** describes an **economic system**.

An economic system is the set of institutions (households, firms, the government) and the arrangements through which a society decides **what** to produce, **how** to produce it and **for whom**, so that scarce resources are turned into finished goods and services and distributed to those who use them. (The excerpt itself also calls it "the economy"; "economic system" is the term that best fits.)

Marking: correct term (2 marks); a brief justification may be given for credit.

questions.enonce_markdown: Apart from the traditional economy, identify two other economic systems. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two other economic systems (1 mark each, any two):

1. **Market (free enterprise or capitalist) economy** - resources are privately owned and the price mechanism, guided by supply and demand and the profit motive, answers the questions of what, how and for whom to produce.
2. **Command (planned or socialist) economy** - resources are owned by the state and a central planning authority takes the main production and distribution decisions.

A **mixed economy**, which combines private enterprise with state intervention, is also acceptable as one of the two systems.

questions.enonce_markdown: What type of economic system exists in Cameroon? Give one reason. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon has a **mixed economy** (2 marks).

**Reason (2 marks, any one well developed):**

- Both the **private sector and the public sector** operate side by side. Most farmers, traders, transporters and firms are privately owned, are free to produce and sell, and most prices are set by supply and demand; at the same time the state owns or controls some public enterprises and key services, regulates markets (for example standards and competition rules), taxes incomes and spends on public goods such as roads, schools and hospitals.

Other acceptable reasons: the government plans development (national development strategies) while leaving most production decisions to private owners; the state intervenes through subsidies, price controls or public ownership in selected sectors.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State two advantages of the economic system identified in (c) above. (4 marks)

(ii) Distinguish an economy from an economic system. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two advantages of a mixed economy (2 marks each, any two, each stated and explained):**

1. **It combines the efficiency of the market with social protection by the state.** Private ownership and the profit motive give firms an incentive to produce efficiently, to innovate and to respond to consumers' wishes, while the government can correct the weaknesses of the market.
2. **The government provides public and merit goods and corrects market failure.** Goods such as roads, security, basic education and health care, which private firms would under-supply, are provided by the state, and the state can control monopolies and externalities such as pollution.
3. **Greater equity and stability.** Taxes and transfer payments reduce extreme inequality, and fiscal policy can be used to smooth fluctuations in output and employment.
4. **Consumer freedom of choice** is kept in most markets, so consumers are not limited to what a central planner decides.

**(ii) Economy and economic system (4 marks):**

- An **economy** is the actual set of productive activities, resources, households, firms and markets of a particular country or region, taken as a whole (for example the economy of Cameroon or the economy of the CEMAC area). It describes **what exists**: the totality of economic activity in a place.
- An **economic system** is the **method or set of rules and institutions** through which a society organises production, distribution and exchange, that is, how it answers the questions of what, how and for whom to produce (market, command, traditional or mixed system). It describes **how the economy is organised and run**.

In short, an economy is a particular country's productive set-up; an economic system is the way it is organised. Different economies (for example those of Cameroon, Nigeria and Kenya) can operate under the same type of economic system (mixed), and the same economy can change its system over time.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two roles played by the government in the economy of Cameroon. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two roles (2 marks each, any two, each stated and explained):

1. **Provision of public goods and services.** The government builds and maintains roads, schools, hospitals, water and electricity networks and provides security and justice, which the private sector would not supply adequately.
2. **Regulation of economic activity.** It makes and enforces laws on competition, prices, standards, labour and the environment, and so protects consumers and workers.
3. **Redistribution of income and welfare.** Through taxes, subsidies and social transfers it reduces inequality and supports the poor.
4. **Promotion of growth and development.** It invests in infrastructure, supports agriculture and industry (for example credit and subsidies to farmers) and attracts investment.
5. **Employer and owner of public enterprises**, and **stabiliser** of the economy through fiscal policy (monetary policy is conducted regionally by the central bank of the CEMAC zone).
